entities.summary: The Ningbo–Taizhou–Wenzhou railway or Yong-Tai-Wen railway is a dual-track, electrified, high-speed rail line in Zhejiang Province, China. It is named after the three prefecture-level cities along route: Ningbo, whose abbreviated Chinese name is Yong, Taizhou and Wenzhou. The line has a total length of 282.4 kilometres (175.5 mi) and forms part of Hangzhou–Fuzhou–Shenzhen railway. Construction began in October 2005, and the line opened to commercial service on September 28, 2009. Trains running on the line reach top speeds of 250 kilometres per hour, and the shortest trip between Ningbo and Wenzhou takes 1 hour 12 minutes.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Ningbo–Taizhou–Wenzhou railway played a significant role in modernizing China's transportation infrastructure, connecting major cities and facilitating economic growth. The line has reduced travel times between key cities by over an hour, contributing to the development of the region.
